prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1092; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant describing a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection. The claimant reports neck pain and stiffness that began shortly after the impact and asked that the claim be opened for bodily injury and vehicle damage.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was active on the reported date of loss. No issues with the policy status were found at this stage.

Entry 3: Reviewed photographs submitted by the claimant showing the rear bumper and tail lamp area of the vehicle. The images confirm some of the damage described, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant about the sequence of events. The account was consistent with the first notice and the claimant repeated the same description of the impact. The claimant could not confirm exactly where in the vehicle they were seated at the moment of impact, so this point remains open.

Entry 5: Requested prior vehicle and medical records. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on file, and no prior injury to the neck or upper back has been identified so far. The reported injury is consistent in type and force with a collision of this kind.

Entry 6: Reviewed the initial medical report. Treatment began with a few visits, but additional services have been added in each month since, and the frequency and scope now exceed what is typical for this kind of injury. The damage estimate has not yet been reconciled with the impact, and it is not yet clear whether all of the damage resulted from this collision.

Entry 7: Sent a request to the treating provider for itemized treatment notes and the clinical reasoning behind the added services. A follow-up call with the claimant confirmed the same account of the collision and of the symptoms, with no new facts introduced.

Entry 8: File remains open pending the provider response and an independent review of the vehicle damage. Nothing so far suggests the damage predates the policy start date, but the scope of the medical treatment and the extent of the vehicle damage still need to be resolved before a settlement position is set.
